subject: Next steps and technical clarifications — hosting mode & migration plan
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jan 2027 14:05:00 -0500
Subject: Recap & clarifying questions — hosting modes and migration constraints

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for taking the call today — appreciated the clear summary of Nimbus's timeline and the constraints from your security and procurement teams. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying items that will help us size options (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) and shape a migration plan from your current vendor (OrionAI) and the legacy GPU cluster you run for batch jobs.

High-level recap:
- Primary goal: reduce inference cost by ~35% while meeting ~80ms 95th percentile latency for chat endpoints.
- Regulatory: HIPAA + state-level data residency preference for production PHI.
- Migration sources: live traffic on OrionAI (real-time) + nightly batch jobs on internal GPU cluster (model is 7B fine-tuned LLaMA lineage).
- Procurement asks: predictable monthly cost for planning; SOC2 evidence; ability to contract for Dedicated capacity or Private deployment.

Clarifying questions (so we can put together accurate pricing and runbook):
1) Peak qps and traffic shape: can you confirm expected concurrent chat sessions (or qps) at peak and the typical request size in tokens (avg/p95)? Any predictable burst windows?
2) KV cache persistence: the internal cluster currently uses a warm-KV cache persisted to NFS between bursts. Do you need RW access to KV persistence on Redwood Dedicated/Private, or would a cold-warm strategy be acceptable?
3) Networking: for Private VPC, will your team require egress-only (no inbound) control plane access, or do you expect to host the control plane inside your VPC entirely (air-gapped/on-prem needs)?
4) Data plane encryption & KMS: do you have an existing KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, etc.) you must integrate with for production keys?
5) Cutover preference: do you want a blue-green (dual-run) cutover for real-time traffic, or is a canary stepwise rollout sufficient?

Attachments: I’ve attached a short Dedicated pricing worksheet and a migration checklist template — those will help once we have the numbers above.

Next steps proposed:
- You respond to the clarifying items above (ideally by Mon 2/2).
- We’ll produce 2 commercial options: (A) Hosted API with caching tweaks + fallback to a smaller Dedicated pool, (B) Reserved Dedicated with optional Private VPC pilot.
- If Private is preferred, Marissa will coordinate SOC2 evidence and a pilot contract template.

Happy to jump on a 20-min follow-up if that’s easier for the team.

Best,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf, migration-checklist.xlsx
From: Emily Torres <emily.torres@nimbushealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jan 2027 16:42:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Recap & clarifying questions — hosting modes and migration constraints

Thanks Sean — useful recap. A few answers and follow-up items below.

Answers:
- Peak: expecting ~120 qps at peak for chat (concurrent sessions ~750). Typical request is small: 40 tokens in, 120 tokens out (avg), p95 output ~350 tokens. Nightly batch runs 10–12 hours with large contexts (up to 2k tokens) for vector indexing rebuilds.
- KV cache: we currently rely on NFS for persistence between runs — for production we prefer persistent KV (so a cold-warm strategy alone will be risky during burst windows).
- Networking: procurement prefers Private VPC with control plane egress-only access to Redwood's managed services. Air-gapped is only for an isolated PI retention system, not for the whole inference pipe.
- KMS: AWS KMS is the standard for us.
- Cutover: will need a blue-green plan for the real-time chat path given compliance testing. Batch can be cut over in windows.

Can you also outline expected downtime or degraded latency windows during cutover for each option (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)? Procurement will need those estimates.

Finally, Alex from procurement will loop in legal for contract preferences — we should expect a couple of standard redlines around indemnity and data residency.

-Emily
Emily Torres
Head of ML Platform, Nimbus Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 31 Jan 2027 02:18:00 -05:00
Subject: Internal: feasibility notes from infra side (for Emily)

Quick internal notes to help craft the reply to Emily tomorrow:
- Latency target (80ms p95) for chat at 120 qps: Hosted API with dynamic batching will probably meet p95 for small requests if we enable prefix caching + dedicated priority lane, but sustained 120 qps with large output p95 (350 tokens) will increase token cost and push us to Dedicated for predictable tail latency.
- KV persistence: we can offer an out-of-the-box Redis-backed persistent KV layer for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted, we'd propose a managed Redis with cross-region replication — but that adds egress/security considerations for Nimbus's VPC rules.
- Cutover impact:
  * Hosted API: minimal downtime (mostly DNS + config switch), but cannot meet strict VPC-only procurement constraints.
  * Dedicated: blue-green possible with staged traffic shift; expect brief (~2–10 minute) elevated latencies during cache warm-up on first sustained traffic, but no full downtime.
  * Private (VPC): depends on whether control plane needs to be egress-only — if we host the control plane egress-only, there is additional setup (~2–3 business days) for secure peering and KMS integration. On-prem full air-gap will require longer (2–4 weeks) and a scoped ops engagement.
- Action: I'll draft a short table with expected latency impact, setup time, and cost delta for each option for Emily.

Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recap & clarifying questions — hosting modes and migration constraints

Emily / Alex — thanks for the fast responses and context.

Next steps (concrete):
1) Karthik will send a concise matrix by EOD Monday that shows: estimated p95 latency (small chat / large token output), cache warm-up behavior, setup lead time, and the delta in monthly cost (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
2) Marissa will share SOC2 evidence and our standard Dedicated pilot contract; she’ll also include a sample Private VPC checklist so procurement can start the network review.
3) Redwood will produce a blue-green cutover runbook for the chat path that includes expected transient latency windows and verification tests for PHI handling.
4) Alex / Nimbus procurement to confirm internal legal contacts and a list of required redlines (we’ll put a draft MSA in HubSpot).

I’ve attached the pricing worksheet and a migration checklist; I’ll follow up with a brief 30-min working session next week to walk through Karthik’s matrix and procurement asks. Would Tue 2/3 at 11am ET work for your team?

Thanks — Sean
